title: Rectangular bar
spec: Create a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees around the X-axis, zero degrees around the Y-axis, and negative ninety degrees around the Z-axis. Ensure the translation vector is set to zero in all directions. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. Begin with the first loop, which consists of four lines. The first line starts at the origin and ends at coordinates (0.75, 0.0). The second line starts at (0.75, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0459). The third line starts at (0.75, 0.0459) and ends at (0.0, 0.0459). Finally, the fourth line completes the loop by starting at (0.0, 0.0459) and ending at the origin. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.75. Transform the scaled sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it with the same vector. Extrude the transformed sketch 0.0459 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular bar are a length of 0.75 units, a width of 0.04591836734693877 units, and a height of 0.04591836734693877 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0459) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0459) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0459)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are -90.0, 0.0, -90.0, which corresponds to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis.
# The translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], so no translation is needed.
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
